A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReWeaver work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including corrections moved from v1's appendix into v2's main tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original GCD-TS reconstruction experiments, comparisons with AIpparel-MV, refinement ablations, and qualitative simulation results, including corrected numerical results in its appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional evaluated comparisons with Sewformer and ChatGarment.

M1.justification: The visual encoder, bi-path transformer, hyper-network geometry decoders, 2D prediction module, losses, and refinement procedures remain unchanged. Appendix E newly explains the simulation workflow without establishing a change to the proposed reconstruction method.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain GCD-TS and four-view reconstruction of garment geometry and sewing patterns. No new dataset or separately evaluated reconstruction scenario is reported; the revised posed renderings illustrate the existing downstream simulation use.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands the principal comparison from AIpparel-MV alone to Sewformer, ChatGarment, and AIpparel, substantially broadening the comparator set. AIpparel is the retained four-view, fine-tuned baseline under a shortened name.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds protocols for the new comparators: four-view inputs, ChatGarment fine-tuning with converted GCD-TS JSON, and Sewformer training using AIpparel's modifications. Existing stated splits, input resolution, and ReWeaver training budget are unchanged. Newly specified panel zero-centering does not establish a revision to the earlier evaluation.

E4.justification: The refinement and adaptive-sampling analyses are retained. v2 Table 3 reproduces v1 Table 6's cumulative refinement ablation, while v2 Table 2 uses results already supplied in v1's correction table. Figure 6 is redrawn without adding ablation conditions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added baseline rows retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds Sewformer and ChatGarment results, including overall accuracies of 0.1806 and 0.4452. ChatGarment leads edge accuracy at 0.8012 versus ReWeaver's 0.7175. ReWeaver's v2 scores already appear in v1's corrected Tables 3–5, so their incorporation into the main tables is not a new performance gain.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the formal dimensionality of 2D edge samples from R^(M_E x 3) to R^(M_E x 2), consistent with the existing decoder. The losses and refinement derivations remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of joint, corresponding 2D–3D reconstruction from as few as four views, the GCD-TS contribution, and superior reconstruction quality. Additional comparisons support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix G revises the earlier limitations discussion to explicitly identify restricted generalization to out-of-distribution and real-world data. Proposed remedies now include varying cameras, human shapes and poses, backgrounds, and incorporating real training data, replacing the earlier emphasis on texture expansion and generative synthesis.

D1.justification: New Appendix E specifies Marvelous Designer, manual panel-placement refinement, predicted sewing relationships, default material parameters, and planned release of simulation project files. Section 4.2 newly specifies panel zero-centering, and the abstract adds a project link promising code and data. These disclosures do not establish that resources have already been released.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 replaces the detailed PhysAvatar discussion with discussion of already-cited Gaussian Garments and adds criticism of DiffAvatar's runtime. Marvelous Designer is newly cited. The additional published Gaussian Garments reference represents the same work as the retained preprint, not a new research contribution.

P1.justification: Localized edits clarify notation, revise related-work and baseline paragraphs, remove the correction notice, and reorganize the appendix with simulation and limitations sections. Most prose remains unchanged. v2 also repeats the full abstract on PDF page 2, introducing conspicuous redundancy.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 3 are extensively redesigned, Figure 4 is reframed around garment close-ups, and Figure 6 becomes a simplified 2D refinement diagram. Table 1 gains comparator rows, the separate correction tables are consolidated into the main tables, and the retained ablation table is renumbered. These substantially revise the central visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The added Sewformer and ChatGarment comparisons broaden empirical context, while the simulation workflow and evaluation disclosures improve transparency. Integrating v1's existing corrections makes the main results easier to interpret, without demonstrating new ReWeaver performance gains. These benefits outweigh the duplicated abstract in v2, but the net improvement remains limited.
